posts.author: wiffle88
posts.body:
Eventing a menu with pictures is actually pretty plausible in RPG Maker.  Eventing something like what you see there is also plausible, it would just take longer.
It really just requires keeping track of your individual pictures that you show, some variables, and some input tracking.
There's actually an official tutorial that should get you pretty close!
Eventing a Picture-Based Menu | The Official RPG Maker Blog
The default RPG Maker menu works well, but sometimes you want one that fits your game’s aesthetic better or offers only the important options. Eventing your own picture-based menu is a great way to make sure your menu fits your game, so let’s take a look at how to make one.
www.rpgmakerweb.com

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body: The unspoken qualifier is how to do this "without scripting" and I just don't see how you can do it without at least intermediate scripting knowledge. Even with Triacontane's plugin that menu has custom datasets you can't just pull from the database. "Villagers" is not a dataset that's part of the RPG Maker engine nor is likes/loves. I guess the easiest way is making the villagers actors with notetags in their notebox to define all the like/love stuff, but you would still have to script to parse those.

I mean that's fair, a plugin would definitely make things easier.  But it could also make things more complicated when you need to do something outside of the scope of the plugin.
I typically see things from an art perspective and then work backwards.  The way I see it, you could pretty easily make some quick boxes in a pixel art program and put the word "Villagers" in one of the top boxes.  You could also save the villager NPC sprites as separate pictures that you input into the custom art assets, or get stored in the Pictures project folder and called when necessary using the Show Picture command.
If you get rid of the scrolling bar and make it a left/right toggle button (easier to do with pure eventing), you could simply call up the pictures you need based on some variables.  (If right, variable "Villager menu counter" + 1.  If left, variable "Village menu counter" - 1, etc.)
Then based on the "Village menu counter" variable, you could simply call the correct pictures, deleting others from the screen as needed.
Friendship levels could also be evented and simply have different heart pictures that get called based on a variable.  Dynamically updating likes and dislikes would take more effort, but the idea is similar.
In fact, each villager could be a common event that the main menu event calls upon to keep things more clean.
Yes, it would be work, but so does any custom menu.  I don't think this would require much, if any scripting.  And it could be scaled up or down depending on how detailed the OP needs it to be.

I could probably mock something up if I find the time.
